To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LiFeCl 3 and AgFeCl3 are obtained by direct synthesis from LiCl or AgCI and FeCl3.
we synthesized two new ionic conductors: AgFeCl 3 and LiFeCl 3.
LiFeCl  and AgFeCl  are obtained by direct reaction of LiCl and AgCl with FeCl at 300 °C and 400 °C, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and the study of the electrical and magnetic properties of the compounds MFeCl4 (M = Li, Na, Ag).
the synthesis, crystal structure, physical and electrochemical properties of new lithium and silver halide based compounds.
the study of the structural, magnetic and ionic transport properties of the new ionic conductors: LiFeCl 3 and AgFeCl3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the silver derivative is a poor conductor of lithium ions in the solid state.
the LiFeCl 3 system is not an ionic conductor, but that the LiFe 1-x Ag x Cl 3 system (x = 1) is an ionic conductor with a low mobility of Li + ions.
the silver compound is an insulating semiconductor and the lithium one an ionic conductor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Li 1+ and Ag 1+ ions in the LiFeCl 3 and AgFeCl3 ionic compounds are not able to stabilize a high spin Fe 3+ ion in a tetrahedral situation, and that the LiFeCl4 compound is a good 1+ ionic conductor.
the ionic conductivity is not correlated with the magnetic behavior.

the silver derivative AgFeCl 3 has a structure isotypic to AgFeCl 2, and is a semiconductor, whereas the lithium derivative LiFeCl 3 crystallizes in a structure isotypical to LiFeS 2, and exhibits metallic behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ionic conductivity of LiFeCl 3 is much higher than that of the other two materials, which is due to the presence of lithium cations that are highly mobile in this material.
the LiFeCl4  and AgFeCl4 compounds are good ionic conductors and could be promising candidates for the development of lithium batteries and other energy storage applications.
the LiFeCl 3 and AgFeCl3 compounds are ionic conductors with a low activation energy, making them good candidates for the development of solid electrolytes for batteries.
